action_context_hypothesised_benefit: Acute rescue of a seizure already under way (endpoint 1).
compound_or_probe: Ketamine and memantine (NMDAR pore blockers; not units of the selection view); d-APV (tool); lithium and ethosuximide (given before the provoking injection, so not rescue).
identity_status: not assessed here (class-level comparison; BLOCK-1 not run)
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO] Nothing is shown to rescue in a WWOX system; the only in-system acute abolition is d-APV on slice bursts (neuron-specific knockout cortical slices, n = 5 slices from 3 animals, one preparation; rebound above baseline after washout). Ketamine has the most paediatric evidence in this niche in other settings (uncontrolled series, one halted refractory-status trial, a positive randomised first-line trial; abstract level; TRANSFER, tier 3); no WOREE child with ketamine was found.
functional_comparison: More promising by general paediatric evidence: ketamine (transfer only). More promising in a WWOX system: none.
mechanism_discriminating_control: A post-onset arm of any agent in a WWOX system.
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: A treatment-after-onset arm in a Wwox-null preparation.
outcome_favourable: A WWOX-system agent that stops an established seizure.
outcome_unresolved: Evidence from other settings does not transfer to the genotype class without a measurement.
explanations_not_separated: Ketamine and memantine are not distinguished from each other in this endpoint by any WWOX datum.

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: Provoked-seizure suppression in a Wwox-null or WWOX-deficient system (endpoint 2).
compound_or_probe: Ethosuximide and lithium (one experiment, one laboratory, one origin); the NMDAR pore blockers have none.
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO] Only lithium and ethosuximide are measured. Lithium is significant in all three genotypes; ethosuximide is significant in the knockout only as a difference in significance; the two arms were tested against different PTZ-alone cohorts (the knockout PTZ-alone curves of the two panels differ in height), so 'lithium better than ethosuximide' is a cross-cohort impression, not a tested difference.
functional_comparison: More promising: lithium and ethosuximide over every other candidate (they are the only ones measured), for different reasons: lithium for a robust effect that is probably general; ethosuximide for the only open selectivity question and the weaker mechanistic rationale.
mechanism_discriminating_control: Genotype-crossed design with a vehicle per genotype, an age series, an assay-sensitivity panel and a non-floor stimulus (the brief).
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: A pilot that fixes variability, assay age and stimulus.
outcome_favourable: An interaction ratio at most 0.7 or at least 1.43 with a valid panel (selective), or between 0.7 and 1.43 (general). [K2 mapping, 2026-11-18, IT, from SCI's in vivo brief section 4 (priors file sha256 326846fb5180), mapped not authored: each pattern is read only where the assay-sensitivity panel is valid at the age and wild type is above the floor. Brief E1: effect ratio in the knockout at most 0.7, wild type null, interaction ratio at most 0.7 -> favours a knockout-selective effect (does not show a T-type route or a spontaneous-seizure benefit). Brief E2: wild type null at the assay age and an effect at an older age -> favours an age-limited effect with a wild-type floor, so the published pattern is not knockout selectivity (does not show that the knockout effect is absent). Brief E3: similar effects in all genotypes, interaction ratio between 0.7 and 1.43 -> favours a general anticonvulsant effect (does not show selectivity or its absence at other ages). Brief C1: a selective T-type blocker beside ethosuximide gives the same pattern in the knockout -> a T-type route is plausible, not proven without engagement or genetics. Any arm: minimal-seizure incidence up while generalised incidence down -> favours a seizure-type-specific action (does not show benefit or harm in the null phenotype). Source: experiment_brief_presidio013_sci_20261116/invivo_pup_adv059_sci_20261118/INVIVO_PUP_EXPERIMENT_BRIEF_V1_SCI_20261118.md]
outcome_contrary: No effect anywhere, or a failed panel. [K2 mapping, 2026-11-18, IT, from SCI's in vivo brief section 4 (priors file sha256 326846fb5180), mapped not authored: Brief E4: no effect anywhere -> the published knockout effect did not replicate at this age and stimulus (says nothing about other ages or exposures). Brief C2: the selective T-type blocker has no effect where ethosuximide has one -> ethosuximide's effect is not carried by selective T-type block at this exposure and age, or the exposure was inadequate (which is not separated). Brief E5: a failed assay-sensitivity panel or a wild type at the floor -> not interpretable at that age. Source: experiment_brief_presidio013_sci_20261116/invivo_pup_adv059_sci_20261118/INVIVO_PUP_EXPERIMENT_BRIEF_V1_SCI_20261118.md]
outcome_unresolved: The interaction cannot be sized at the published variability.
explanations_not_separated: Lithium and ethosuximide share one origin (ORG-2); the cross-cohort comparison is untested.

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: Chronic seizure control in children of the genotype class (endpoint 4).
compound_or_probe: Vigabatrin, the ketogenic diet, memantine, ethosuximide, ketamine.
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO, aggregate, case-level] Vigabatrin exposure is documented in 22 children in 10 reports (21 to 26 distinct at most; no child is documented as receiving vigabatrin alone with a known full regimen; a response is stated for 11, 8 responses and 3 non-responses, every response qualified): the data bear only 'reported' (blind recount, ADV-062). Randomised evidence for vigabatrin is spasm-defined (infantile spasms) and transfers poorly to other seizure types; the harm side transfers (labelled irreversible visual-field loss, with a labelled caution for pre-existing visual damage; infant MRI change mostly asymptomatic and reversible). Memantine: one randomised crossover trial in childhood developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (abstract and registry), seizure worsening in some GRIN gain-of-function individuals. Ethosuximide: no datum under 3 years (label), school-age cohorts in related syndromes.
functional_comparison: More promising: vigabatrin for spasm control by evidence level in a related seizure type; the ketogenic diet and vigabatrin are the only candidates with class case reports; no ordering for other seizure types; vigabatrin is the heaviest on harm.
mechanism_discriminating_control: A prospective aggregate collection of start age, co-therapy timing and instrumented outcome (clinical channel).
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: Aggregate questions to a clinician or registry (counts only, bands, cells under 3 merged).
outcome_favourable: A clinically instrumented response under a single agent change.
outcome_contrary: Every response remains an impression with co-therapy.
outcome_unresolved: Remission with age, co-therapy, reporting bias and regression to the mean.
explanations_not_separated: Children overlap across the four drug classes; class counts are not additive.
source_locator_depth: ADV-053 section 4; ADV-056 and ADV-062; ADV-058 unit 1; decisive D11

compound_or_probe: AAV9 gene addition (comparator); lithium (conditional); the KCC2 branch and an NKCC1 blocker (hypothesis-level, other models).
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO] Only AAV9 gene addition is measured on development endpoints in the null mouse (survival, weight, motor score, GFAP, myelination structure improved but not normalised); it is prevention or early window, one laboratory, a high-dose row still to be adjudicated. The KCC2 branch (OV350, pup dosing p10 to p21, adult outcomes in a Cdkl5 knockout; one open full text, company-funded, small, unreplicated, text and supplement conflicts) Development: not rankable between the KCC2 and NKCC1 branches; neither has Wwox data. KCC2 side: one sponsor-funded Cdkl5 pup dataset (a shift in timing of a self-resolving phenotype and adult effects, litters randomised, no wild-type-on-agent group). NKCC1 side: neonatal studies in other genetic models with durable outcomes (Kv7 with controls unaffected; Fmr1; Dravet behaviour without seizure effect) and adverse signals (R43Q pro-seizure hazard; a two-genotype social reduction). All abstract or single-paper level. [WITHDRAWN 2026-11-18 by SCI (ADV-065c, after an independent verifier): the statement that the KCC2 branch is more promising than an NKCC1 blocker on development on evidence level only]. Against the other candidates it is not rankable (their development data were not searched). Neither branch is more promising overall; both are gated by the same unmeasured E_GABA and KCC2 state in a WWOX preparation.
functional_comparison: More promising: AAV9 gene addition, clearly, with its limits. Others: not rankable.
mechanism_discriminating_control: A separate in vivo cohort for lithium on the AAV9 comparator's own endpoints, only after a selective lithium effect in the provoked assay (the fallback in the brief addendum 9.1).
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: E_GABA by perforated patch at matched maturity (WO-18, IT57-Q01) before any chloride-branch arm.
outcome_favourable: A development endpoint moved by a non-gene agent in the null pup.
outcome_contrary: Nothing moved, or an early floor (untreated knockouts die by about day 17).
outcome_unresolved: Prevention against rescue; durability; pup exposure.
explanations_not_separated: The development endpoints are confounded by the provoking injection of the provoked-seizure assay.

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: Harms in children and the hardest harm of each candidate (endpoint 6).
compound_or_probe: AAV9; ethosuximide; lithium; the NMDAR pore blockers; vigabatrin; the ketogenic diet; an NKCC1 blocker; the KCC2 branch.
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO, label and abstract level] AAV9: no overexpression or tumour endpoint (irreversible risk unmeasured). Ethosuximide: blood dyscrasias, immune-mediated reactions; not established below 3 years. Lithium: toxicity close to therapeutic concentrations, renal and thyroid effects; no infant treatment data. Pore blockers: seizure aggravation (memantine in three named GRIN gain-of-function individuals; drug-provoked seizures after ketamine), developing-brain apoptosis signal in rat (TRANSFER). Vigabatrin: irreversible visual-field loss, a labelled caution with pre-existing visual damage, infant MRI change; myelin and retinal lesions in young rodents. NKCC1 blocker: ototoxicity signals and a neonatal trial stopped early for harm. [ADV-079 mapping, 2026-11-19, IT, from SCI's note as corrected (advisor_pilot_20261113/brainstorm_20261116/harm_against_phenotype_adv079_sci_20261119/HARM_AGAINST_PHENOTYPE_ADV079_SCI_20261119.md sections 4.5 and 5), mapped not authored: harm cells that move: vigabatrin retina and optic PARTIAL (blind verifier; first delivered YES), vigabatrin brain size, myelin and peripheral nerve YES, ethosuximide liver and kidney, pore blockers hepatobiliary (thin), lithium kidney PARTIAL; 13 intersections (5 YES, 8 PARTIAL); a NO is a keyword absence, not a safety statement; vigabatrin ALT and AST unreliable (label); a vigabatrin visual readout needs a drug-free baseline (optic atrophy in 8 of 14 children in four held reports).]
functional_comparison: No candidate is better characterised in WWOX children; harm columns are not ranked.
mechanism_discriminating_control: Harm endpoints of the drug's own (myelin, retina, brain size, renal and thyroid readouts as the label lists) in any development cohort.
measurement_that_makes_it_interpretable: Aggregate clinical questions on symptomatic or resolved imaging change and visual assessment.
outcome_favourable: Harms measured with the efficacy endpoint.
outcome_unresolved: Populations and evidence levels differ across agents.

action_context_hypothesised_benefit: Age window of each candidate (design variable of every in vivo experiment).
compound_or_probe: Valproate, ketamine, memantine, MK-801, GluN2B-selective agents, phenobarbital, diazepam, lithium, GSK-3 inhibitors, T-type blockers other than ethosuximide, ethosuximide, vigabatrin.
documented_action_and_limits: [DATO, abstract level, mostly rat, about half one Prague laboratory family] Valproate protects against PTZ at every age tested in the rat (mouse not found); ketamine suppresses generalised tonic-clonic seizures in rat pups with moderate or no effect on minimal seizures and ataxia at the lowest dose, more in younger animals; memantine and MK-801 suppress generalised seizures and RAISE minimal seizures at young ages; GluN2B-selective agents fade across the window (mouse ifenprodil effective at P7 and P10, not at P14 or P21); phenobarbital efficacious from P10 in the mouse; diazepam is NOT age-flat in the rat (status epilepticus not stopped at P9, stopped at P15 and P21); lithium and GSK-3 inhibitors and the selective T-type blockers: no age-window provoked-seizure paper found by two routes. The Kasahara 2019 mouse inference (P11 against P14, 'undone by bumetanide') is WITHDRAWN: full text shows incidence not raised, latency effect not blocked, all high-dose diazepam mice dead at P11 and P14, groups of 4 to 5.
functional_comparison: No ordering; the age window is a design variable.
mechanism_discriminating_control: An age series of wild-type pups with an assay-sensitivity panel.
outcome_favourable: Efficacy that differs by age within the experiment window.
explanations_not_separated: Seizure type per animal separates agents that move minimal and generalised seizures in opposite directions.
